rationale: The route CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→USER→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP is followed exactly as stated, and 'multiple' mode is justified: cross-checking the full message table against user_teams roles confirms exactly two admin-authored channels (engineering and general, both via Robert Walsh, the only message-posting admin; the other admin, Morgan Freeman, authored no messages anywhere). No other channel's posters hold admin/owner role, so no hidden extra matches exist. Negatives are well-chosen and path-derived: admin_without_messages breaks the MESSAGE link despite satisfying the role condition, negative_random_channel/negative_growth_channel show active channels failing purely on role, and negative_member_author demonstrates that a member posting in already-qualifying channels doesn't add or remove matches, testing correct handling of mixed-role channels. Answer_attributes are bare table.column names, and the access_plan (conversations.list + conversations.history + users.info/user_teams) reflects real, documented API capabilities without inventing relations. The only minor gap is that no 'owner' role example exists in the seed to exercise that branch of the disjunction, but this is not required since admin alone already validates the logic and exhaustive combination coverage isn't mandated.
